title: Order book
text: Order by order data tells you about every single order on the book. Building the book from it takes two data structures, and a handful of rules that must be exactly right.

title: Why order by order
text: A price level feed gives you totals. An order by order feed, like Nasdaq ITCH, gives you every order: its reference number, side, size and price. From that you rebuild the levels yourself, and you also see each order arrive, shrink and leave. The cost is volume. Every add, execution, cancel and delete is a message you must apply, in order.

title: Two structures
text: The lab's book builder keeps two structures. An order map, from reference number to the order: price, remaining shares, stock locate and side. And for each instrument, two sorted vectors of price levels, with the best price at the back. Each level holds a price, an order count and total shares. Almost all activity is near the touch, so a scan from the back usually stops within a few levels.

title: The rules
text: The rules come from the ITCH spec. Add, and add with attribution, insert an order. Executed, and executed with price, reduce it. An order executed down to zero leaves the book with no delete message. Cancel reduces, and delete removes. Replace removes the original order and adds a new reference, with the same side and stock. Trade, cross and broken trade messages never touch the visible book.

title: Worked example
text: One stock. Add order 11: buy 300 at 50.10. Add order 12: buy 200 at 50.10. The level now holds two orders and 500 shares. Execute 100 shares of order 11, and the level drops to 400. Replace order 12 with order 13: 200 shares at 50.11. A new best bid appears, and 50.10 is down to one order. Delete order 11, and the 50.10 level is gone.

title: The order map
text: The order map is an open addressing table with linear probing. Its hash is the identity. In the lab's notes, reference numbers come in sequence through the day, and most orders are cancelled soon after they are added. So live orders sit in a window of recent numbers, and land in adjacent slots. A multiplicative hash measured about 35 percent slower on the lab's book rebuild. Deletes shift later entries back, so no tombstones pile up.

title: Checks
text: Every rule has a check. An update for an unknown reference, a reused reference, more shares executed than remain, and a level that disagrees with its orders are all counted. A digest of every level proves a live feed rebuilt exactly the books a file replay did. One honest gap: adding a level can still grow a vector, so a live book should reserve its levels at startup.

title: Takeaway
text: An order map and sorted levels, kept in step by the spec's rules, and checked on every message.
